潘杜拉琴屬弦鳴，為古希臘中長頸魯特，小音箱，常三弦，也稱三弦琴。名稱可追溯至蘇美: The pandura is a chordophone, a medium-long-necked lute of ancient Greece with a small soundbox, usually with three strings, hence also called the three-string. The name can be traced to the Sumerian for 'small bow'; when a resonator was added to the bow and the bow straightened, it became the lute. Mesopotamia had lute-type instruments from the Akkadian period or the third millennium BCE; Greek art depicts such instruments from the third or fourth century BCE. In the Roman period the neck was widened to take four strings, and the body was mostly oval or slightly wider at the bottom. It later spread to the Near East, eastern Europe, North Africa and the Balkans, giving rise to the Georgian panduri, the Greek tambura and bouzouki, the North African kuitra, the eastern Mediterranean saz and the Balkan tamburica. Renato Meucci (1996) considers that some Italian descendants of the Renaissance instrument were called the Italian guitar, mandore or mandola.
潘杜拉琴是古希臘的弦鳴樂器，屬於廣義魯特琴與吉他樂器家族。其形制為中長頸魯特琴，: The pandura is a chordophone of ancient Greece, belonging to the lute and guitar family in the broad sense. It is a medium-long-necked lute with a small soundbox, usually with three strings, which is why it is also called the three-string. The ancient Greeks used instruments of this kind; in the Roman period the long neck was kept but widened to take four strings, and the body was oval or slightly wider at the bottom. The Akkadians of Mesopotamia also played a similar instrument, from which related instruments developed in the Caucasus, Greece, North Africa and the Balkans.
潘杜拉琴琴身採用共鳴腔設計，通常由優質木材製成，包括桃花心木或紫檀等硬木。琴頸細: The body of the pandura has a resonating cavity and is usually made of good timber, including hardwoods such as mahogany or rosewood. The neck is slender, mostly of maple or oak, so that the fingers can move freely on the strings. The strings were originally of sheep gut or silk; later metal strings may have been used to make the timbre more penetrating. The surface of the body may be decorated with ivory or shell inlay. The soundboard is of spruce or another softwood, to improve the sound.
潘杜拉琴音色明亮清透，具有獨特的金屬質感與穿透力。其音域屬於中高音區域，音色輕盈: The pandura has a bright, clear timbre with a distinctive metallic quality and penetration. Its range lies in the middle and upper register, and the sound is light and agile, suited to quick, lively melodic lines. Its resonance depends on the cavity inside the body and the sympathetic vibration of the strings, which gives a relatively simple, direct sound. Beside the warm thickness of the modern guitar, the pandura is finer and more transparent; beside the soft restraint of the lute, it sounds more alive and more tense. Because the structure is compact and the neck slender, the overtones the vibrating strings produce are rich and clear, and the sound overall has a classical elegance: it keeps the warmth of a string instrument while showing a firm, strong plucking attack.
